text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) regulates food products under the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006. For AYUSH sector, FSSAI relevance: Ayurvedic food supplements, nutraceuticals, herbal teas, functional foods, and health foods fall under FSSAI jurisdiction (NOT D&C Act) if they don't claim to treat/cure diseases. Key distinction: products making therapeutic claims = drugs (D&C Act). Products for nutrition/wellness without disease claims = food (FSSAI). FSSAI license is mandatory for all food businesses with annual turnover above Rs 12 lakh.

FSSAI licensing based on business scale: 1) Registration (FSSAI Basic) — petty food businesses with turnover up to Rs 12 lakh/year, home-based food businesses. Fee: Rs 100/year. 2) State License — medium businesses with turnover Rs 12 lakh to Rs 20 crore/year, manufacturing units. Fee: Rs 2,000-5,000/year based on capacity. 3) Central License — large businesses with turnover above Rs 20 crore, importers/exporters, multi-state operations. Fee: Rs 7,500/year. For AYUSH food businesses: most require State License; exporters need Central License. Apply online at foscos.fssai.gov.in.

FSSAI defines nutraceuticals as foods providing health benefits beyond basic nutrition. Food Safety and Standards (Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals, Foods for Special Dietary Uses, etc.) Regulations 2016 govern this sector. Categories: 1) Health supplements — vitamins, minerals, amino acids, probiotics. 2) Nutraceuticals — functional ingredients providing physiological benefit. 3) Foods for special dietary uses — diabetic foods, gluten-free foods. 4) Foods for special medical purposes — enteral nutrition. For AYUSH nutraceuticals: use only ingredients permitted in Schedule II-VII. Novel ingredients require FSSAI approval. Claims must follow Schedule IV guidelines.

FSSAI regulates health claims on food products. Schedule IV of FSS (Advertising and Claims) Regulations 2018 lists permitted claims. Categories: 1) Nutrient content claims ('high in Vitamin C', 'source of protein'), 2) Nutrient function claims ('calcium supports bone health'), 3) Reduction of disease risk claims (limited, requires substantiation), 4) Non-addition claims ('no added sugar'). NOT permitted: cure/treatment claims (makes it a drug), comparative claims without evidence, endorsements by FSSAI/government, claims about children unless permitted. For AYUSH foods: use nutrient function claims, avoid therapeutic language.

Food labeling under FSS (Packaging and Labeling) Regulations 2011: Mandatory: product name, list of ingredients (descending order by weight), net quantity, name and address of manufacturer/importer, FSSAI license number with logo, lot/batch number, date of manufacture/packaging, best before date, nutritional information, allergen declaration (if applicable), vegetarian/non-vegetarian logo, instructions for use, MRP. Additional for health supplements/nutraceuticals: warning statements, suggested use, 'not for medicinal use' disclaimer if applicable. Label language: English and one regional language.

Food fortification (adding micronutrients) is encouraged by FSSAI through Food Safety and Standards (Fortification of Foods) Regulations 2018. Fortifiable foods: rice, wheat flour, edible oil, milk, salt, double-fortified salt. Mandatory fortification standards specify levels of vitamins/minerals (e.g., Vitamin A, D, B12, iron, folic acid). Fortified products can use '+F' logo. For AYUSH food manufacturers: fortification can enhance product appeal and nutrition profile. Must follow specified levels — over-fortification is non-compliant. Testing required to verify fortification levels.

Importing food products into India: 1) FSSAI Central License mandatory for all food importers. 2) Importer must register imported products on FSSAI's Food Import Clearance System (FLRS). 3) At port: customs sampling and testing by FSSAI-notified labs. 4) Non-conforming products rejected or re-exported. Required documents: Bill of Entry, invoice, packing list, Certificate of Analysis, health certificate from origin country, FSSAI license copy. For AYUSH ingredient imports: ensure ingredients are permitted in India (check Positive List in regulations), especially for novel/exotic herbs. Non-permitted ingredients require prior FSSAI approval.

FSSAI Food Recall Guidelines mandate recall procedures for unsafe food. Triggers: contamination discovered, labeling errors, consumer complaints, regulatory notification. Classification: Class I (serious health hazard, immediate recall), Class II (may cause illness but not serious), Class III (not health hazard but violates regulations). Process: identify affected batches, notify FSSAI, issue public notice, retrieve products from market, document and destroy unsafe products. For AYUSH food businesses: maintain traceability (link products to batches, suppliers, distributors), have recall plan ready, train staff on recall procedures, keep customer complaint records.

Organic food in India regulated by FSSAI under Food Safety and Standards (Organic Foods) Regulations 2017. Certification required from: 1) NPOP (National Programme for Organic Production) certifying bodies, or 2) PGS-India (Participatory Guarantee System) for farmer groups. Organic products must display: FSSAI logo, certifying body name, certification number, Jaivik Bharat logo. Import: organic imports must have equivalence certificate from recognized country systems or be certified by NPOP-accredited body. For AYUSH organic products: source from certified organic farms, maintain chain of custody documentation, verify certification authenticity before claiming 'organic'.

FSSAI compliance framework: 1) License and Registration — maintain valid FSSAI license, renew before expiry, update details if business changes. 2) Hygiene and Safety — follow Schedule 4 (hygienic and sanitary practices), implement HACCP/ISO 22000 for large operations. 3) Standards Compliance — products must meet FSS standards for quality and safety. 4) Labeling Compliance — accurate labels per regulations. 5) Annual Return — file annual return on FoSCoS portal by May 31. Non-compliance consequences: penalties from Rs 25,000 to Rs 10 lakh, license suspension/cancellation, product seizure, prosecution for serious violations.

Decision framework for AYUSH products — Drug or Food? DRUG (D&C Act) if: therapeutic claims (cure, treat, prevent disease), formulation matches Schedule E reference, dosage form suggests medicine (tablets, capsules, syrups with dosage instructions), intended for medical use. FOOD (FSSAI) if: nutrition/wellness claims only, presented as food supplement, no therapeutic claims, consumed for nutritional benefit. Gray areas: consult CDSCO and FSSAI for clarification. Wrong classification risk: marketed as food but has drug claims — penalty under both acts. Safe approach: if in doubt, apply for drug license (stricter but covers more claims).
